origins.section: 2.2 The Server Reads With Its Packager, the Client With Its Own
2.3 The Client Finds Your Answer by the Fields You Echo

gates.says: all 4 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-layout-one-way: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-layout-one-way: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-layout-one-way: Section 2.2 says the two layouts encode fields 2, 3, 4, 7, 11, 41 and 49 identically, but field 39 is two characters in 1987 and three digits in 1993, so the server packs `000`, the client reads `00`, field 41 comes back shifted, the answer matches nothing and the client gets null, which decides d.
recorded.prompt:q-built-from-scratch: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-built-from-scratch: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-built-from-scratch: Section 2.3 builds the default key from the mapped MTI, field 41 padded to 16 characters and field 11, says an answer with no field 41 'matches nothing', and the output shows 'client got: null', while the opening and 2.3 say the client then sends an 0420 reversal, which decides c.
recorded.prompt:q-advice-answered-as-purchase: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-advice-answered-as-purchase: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-advice-answered-as-purchase: Section 2.4 shows '0220 answered with 0210: null, unhandled' and explains that the client keyed its 0220 with `022` while an 0210's key starts with `020` (the 0200's prefix, per 2.3's mapping of 021 to 020), so the unacknowledged advice goes out again as an 0221, which decides c.
recorded.prompt:q-repeat-answer: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-repeat-answer: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-repeat-answer: Section 2.4 states that setResponseMTI drops the repeat flag 'so the 0421 repeat of a reversal gets an 0430', and that the key uses only the MTI's first three digits 'so the 0430 matches the 0421', which decides c.

gates.says: all 12 of this quiz's discriminating readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-layout-one-way:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-layout-one-way:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-layout-one-way:a: Section 2.2 shows that the server reading every request field correctly ('It does, field for field') still leaves the answer garbled by field 39, ending in 'client got: null after 1000 ms'.
recorded.prompt:q-layout-one-way:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-layout-one-way:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-layout-one-way:b: The 2.8 stock-layouts table gives both iso87ascii and iso93ascii as ASCII digits with 16 hex characters per 64 bits, yet 2.2 shows the answer misread because of field 39, so a shared format and bitmap do not prevent the mismatch.
recorded.prompt:q-layout-one-way:c: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-layout-one-way:c: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-layout-one-way:c: Section 2.2 answers 'Does the server read the next purchase?' with 'It does, field for field', and the 'server got:' line shows the request unpacked correctly.
recorded.prompt:q-built-from-scratch:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-built-from-scratch:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-built-from-scratch:a: Section 2.3's key breakdown ('field 41 padded to 16 characters, then field 11') and the 'built from scratch' output, where a response copying field 11 still gets null, show the key is more than field 11 and the MTI.
recorded.prompt:q-built-from-scratch:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-built-from-scratch:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-built-from-scratch:b: Section 2.3 says field 37 joins the key only 'on a link whose QMUX sets <key>41, 11, 37</key>', and the default key it spells out has field 41 and field 11 but not 37.
recorded.prompt:q-built-from-scratch:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-built-from-scratch:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-built-from-scratch:d: Section 2.3's reading of the default key (out queue, mapped MTI, field 41, field 11) does not include field 42.
recorded.prompt:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:a: Section 2.4 says an 0210's key starts with `020` while the 0220 was keyed with `022`, so it 'matches nothing even with every field echoed'.
recorded.prompt:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:b: Sections 2.3 and 2.4 say the key keeps the MTI's first three digits and maps only the response digit (021 to 020), so 020 and 022 differ and the answer is not accepted.
recorded.prompt:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-advice-answered-as-purchase:d: By inference: section 2.4 gives the cause of the mismatch as the key prefix (`022` against `020`) 'even with every field echoed', not how the MTI was set, so the failure comes from the key and not from a hand-set MTI being rejected.
recorded.prompt:q-repeat-answer:a: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-repeat-answer:a: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-repeat-answer:a: Section 2.4's table ('0421 -> 0430') and the 2.8 reference (the fourth digit becomes 0 for anything other than 2-5) show the answer is an 0430, not an 0431.
recorded.prompt:q-repeat-answer:b: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-repeat-answer:b: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-repeat-answer:b: Section 2.4 shows the answer is an 0430 and that the client's key uses only the first three digits, which refutes both parts of b.
recorded.prompt:q-repeat-answer:d: the page and the question, and nothing else
recorded.pass:q-repeat-answer:d: independent readers: one with the page (Q1, Q3), one with the question's text only (Q2)
recorded.outcome:q-repeat-answer:d: Section 2.4 states that the client's key uses only the MTI's first three digits, 'so the 0430 matches the 0421'.
